posts.title: Anatomy of a Test
posts.description: Sometimes when talking about testing, I think we have a tendency to resort to broad ideas and jargon without sufficiently explaining what these things might look like in practice. posts.title: Pushing and Pulling: Three Reactivity Algorithms
posts.description: It’s looking like I’m going to need to build a reactive engine for work, so I’m going to prepare for that by writing down what I know about them. I want to look at three ways of building reactive engines: push reactivity, pull reactivity, and the hybrid push/pull combination that is used in a bunch of web frameworks. posts.title: Additional Thoughts about the Command Pattern
posts.description: A couple of weeks ago, I wrote a post on my employer’s blog titled Undo, Redo, and the Command Pattern , which I ended up quite pleased with. Here, I wanted to add a couple of additional thoughts based on some of the discussions and things I’ve read since writing that post. Firstly, undo/redo isn’t the only use for the command pattern! This is something I wish I’d made more explicit in that post.
